exposure: Gestational age at delivery (<36 weeks vs. ≥36 weeks)
cohort: 57 pregnancies with prenatally diagnosed vasa previa
finding: This study found that delivery at or after 36 weeks of gestation in asymptomatic patients with prenatally diagnosed vasa previa was associated with improved neonatal outcomes, including higher birth weight, shorter hospital stay, and lower rates of complications.
mod_finding: All cases were delivered by cesarean section.
gest_age: Mean gestational age: 35.08 weeks (<36 weeks group), 36.11 weeks (≥36 weeks group)
birth_weight: Mean birth weight: 2292.5 g (<36 weeks group), 2774 g (≥36 weeks group)
